rules.title: Method receiver peels surplus reference layers
rules.statement: For a method call `r.m(...)`, if the receiver type is a (non-raw) reference-like type whose pointee is itself reference-like (`&&T`, `&&mut T`, etc.), the extra reference layers are removed by explicit derefs until a single reference layer remains: `r.m()` for `r:&&T` ≡ `(*r).m()`. Raw pointers (`*const`/`*mut`) are not peeled here.

rules.title: Vec::get of a non-Copy element is rejected
rules.statement: `v.get(i)` on a receiver resolving (through one reference layer) to `Vec<E>` where `E` is a non-Copy (move) type is an error: it would move an element out of borrowed Vec storage, aliasing and double-freeing on drop. The fix is `.borrow(i)` for `&E`, or `.remove(..)`/`.pop()` to take ownership. Copy elements are permitted.
rules.divergence: Mirrors Rust's E0507 'cannot move out of index'; scoped here to Vec::get.

rules.title: Method resolution autoderefs through Deref/DerefMut
rules.statement: If the receiver is a struct with no direct method named `m` (no candidate keyed by concrete or base struct name), and the struct implements `Deref<Target>`, the receiver is dereferenced to `Target` and resolution retries; iterated up to a fixed bound (16). A method defined on the outer type always wins over a Deref-target method.

rules.title: Per-step DerefMut chosen when target method needs &mut self
rules.statement: At each autoderef step, if the Deref target has a candidate method `m` whose first parameter is `&mut Self` and the receiver type implements DerefMut, the mutable DerefMut step is taken so the resulting receiver is a mutable place (`&mut Target`) rather than the shared `&Target` an immutable Deref would yield. Falls back to Deref when no DerefMut impl exists.

rules.title: Method-level turbofish supplies explicit type args
rules.statement: A method call may carry an explicit turbofish `recv.m::<T1,T2>(args)`; the supplied type arguments become the method's type parameters and downstream per-arg type-param inference from argument types is bypassed.

rules.title: len() on a fixed array is a compile-time constant
rules.statement: `a.len()` where `a` has fixed-array type `[T; N]` evaluates to the compile-time size `N` as an `i64` literal; no runtime call is emitted.
rules.divergence: Result type is i64 (Logos stdlib uses i64 for lengths), not usize as in Rust.

rules.title: Method call through a raw pointer requires unsafe
rules.statement: Dispatching a method when the receiver type is a raw pointer (`*const`/`*mut`), including `*mut dyn Trait`/`*const dyn Trait`, requires an `unsafe` context; outside `unsafe` it is an error. The raw pointer is peeled to its pointee for dispatch.

rules.title: Method on a bounded type parameter resolves via its trait bounds
rules.statement: If the receiver (after peeling one reference/raw-pointer layer) is a type parameter `T` (or, conditionally, an associated-type projection), the method is resolved against the traits in `T`'s declared bounds; the concrete impl is selected later during monomorphization.

rules.title: Bounded-type method search walks the supertrait DAG
rules.statement: Method lookup on a bounded type parameter searches each bound trait and, transitively, its supertraits (depth-first, with cycle/diamond guarding). Substitutions compose along supertrait references: a supertrait reference's type-args (written in the sub-trait's namespace incl. Self) are resolved through the current substitution and bound to the supertrait's formal params.

rules.title: Method matching multiple bound traits is ambiguous
rules.statement: When a method name `m` is provided by two distinct traits reachable from a type parameter's bounds (e.g. `trait Foo: A + B` where both A and B define `m`), the call is an error: method `m` is ambiguous (matches both traits). All supertrait siblings are searched so the ambiguity is detected rather than silently resolving to one.

rules.title: Associated-type receiver intercepted only for a non-default method
rules.statement: A method call whose receiver is an associated-type projection `G::R` is dispatched via the assoc-type's declared bounds (`type R: HasId`) only when those bounds supply a NON-default method of that name; if the only provider is a default method (e.g. via a blanket impl), dispatch defers to the ordinary path.

rules.title: Blanket extension trait holds transitively on a bounded type param
rules.statement: If `impl<U: B> Ext for U {}` exists and the receiver type parameter `T` satisfies bound `B` (directly or via a supertrait of one of its bounds) and all the blanket impl's extra bounds, then `T: Ext` holds and `Ext`'s methods (including defaults) are searched for the call.

rules.title: Calling an unsafe trait method requires unsafe
rules.statement: Calling a trait method declared `unsafe` outside an `unsafe` context is an error.

rules.title: Method call argument count must match
rules.statement: A method call must supply exactly (param count − 1) explicit arguments (excluding the `self` receiver); a mismatch is an error.

rules.title: Method type params inferred by unifying params with arg types
rules.statement: Absent turbofish, a trait method's type parameters are inferred by unifying each substituted formal parameter type (seeded with Self → receiver type and any supertrait-derived bindings) against the corresponding argument's type.

rules.title: Method arguments coerced in canonical order
rules.statement: Each method argument is coerced toward its substituted parameter type in canonical order applying: unsize-to-dyn, implicit reborrow, and integer widening. After coercion, a non-Error/non-TypeVar/non-AssocType param type that is incompatible with the argument type is a type-mismatch error.

rules.title: Integer-literal method args range-checked against param type
rules.statement: An integer-literal argument (including elements of array/tuple literals, recursively through nested arrays and tuples) passed to a method parameter of a concrete integer type must fit that type; an out-of-range value is an error.
